title: The quasi-isomorphic augmentation for the finite-free scalar comparison
statement: The point-pulled finite-free augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the exact degree-zero single-complex functor to hS. The result is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes. Mathlib CochainComplex.mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex then proves that the specified monoCokernelAugmentation S is a quasi-isomorphism; this is definitionally the canonical cone augmentation, so no comparison or choice of augmentation is needed.

proof.text: Extract preservation of finite limits and finite colimits by pointUpperStar from profinite_point_pullback. Compose it with the exact geometric inverse image along toSpecZ Z. Finite limits and finite colimits of internal modules are computed on underlying abelian sheaves, so the resulting pointPull Λ Z is exact. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology transports the quasi-isomorphism of step 1 through its degreewise complex functor. By the definition of augmentation this is precisely the asserted morphism. No finite-free presentations, tensor comparison, or K-flatness are needed for this augmentation-only claim.
